question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{2x+3} & \,0\le x\le 1,\,x+1\le y\le x+2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y<2\,|\,X=\frac{3}{4}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<2\,|\,X=\frac{3}{4}) & ={\int }_{1+x}^{2}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\frac{3}{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1+3/4}^{2}\frac{2y}{(2\cdot \frac{3}{4}+3)}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{\int }_{7/4}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}[{y}^{2}]_{7/4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(4-\frac{49}{16}) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$
